title: Nettle and Mr. Hugs' Flower Gift
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a sunny forest where the trees whispered to the wind and the air smelled of pine needles and damp earth, lived a very busy squirrel named Nettle. Nettle had the quickest paws and the brightest eyes you could see. His greatest joy was collecting all sorts of wonderful things: shiny pebbles that sparkled like little stars, fallen feathers brushed with soft colours, and especially the smooth, perfectly rounded cups that held acorns. He’d line them up in his cozy nest, a treasure box of forest wonders, each piece holding a memory of a sunny afternoon or a rustling leaf.

And every day, not too far away, in a little cottage nestled among the ferns, sat Mr. Hugs. Mr. Hugs was a teddy bear, a very special one indeed. His fur was as soft as dandelion fluff, and his button eyes seemed to hold all the warmth in the world. Mr. Hugs’ favourite thing was being a good friend. He would often sit by his window, plush paws resting on the sill, watching the world go by — the flutter of butterflies, the busy march of ants, the distant call of a bird. He was always ready with a comforting presence, a silent promise of a warm embrace.

Until one day, Nettle, while scurrying among the branches, noticed something unusual. Iorwen the badger, who usually said hello with a rumble as he walked by, his striped face looking friendly and awake, was sleeping deeper than ever in his burrow. His nose twitched ever so slightly, a tiny sign of his dreams, but otherwise he seemed lost in a very long, peaceful nap. Nettle’s bright eyes blinked, his twitchy nose testing the air. Iorwen always looked so strong and kind, a good friend in the forest, but Nettle’s tummy did a little flip-flop. He wondered if even a strong badger like Iorwen would like a happy surprise.

“Hmm,” Nettle chittered, bushy tail giving a thoughtful flick. “Iorwen is so good to us all. He always shares the juiciest berries. What if we made him a little treat? Something to make him smile when he wakes up?”

Because of that, Nettle couldn’t bake a cake, and Iorwen wouldn’t want nuts; he liked roots and berries and plump grubs. Nettle scampered down from his grand oak tree, his mind buzzing with ideas. He looked at his treasured collection of acorn cups, so perfectly shaped and smooth, like tiny bowls. Then his gaze drifted toward the meadow nearby, a place always full of cheerful colours and the sweet smell of wildflowers. An idea started to grow, like the flowers he saw.

Mr. Hugs, from his quiet window perch, saw Nettle darting about with a determined glint in his bright little eyes. Mr. Hugs, with his quiet wisdom and his gentle heart, understood. He knew that Nettle’s busy energy often led to wonderful things. Mr. Hugs carefully picked a few of the most vibrant flower petals from the windowsill planter. He chose the softest pinks, the sunniest yellows, and the deepest violets. These petals smelled sweet and calming, like a whispered lullaby on a summer evening.

Because of that, Nettle, with his quick nimble paws, gathered the prettiest, tidiest acorn cups he could find. Smooth and clean, perfectly shaped little bowls, each one unique. Mr. Hugs arrived, his soft paws holding a delicate bouquet of petals, button eyes twinkling with shared purpose. Together they tiptoed, so softly that even the moss on the ground barely noticed, toward Iorwen’s burrow.

They worked side-by-side, a perfect team. Nettle carefully arranged the acorn cups in a neat little cluster just outside the entrance to Iorwen’s home. Mr. Hugs, with the utmost care, placed a vibrant flower petal inside each one, like tiny colourful jewels waiting to be discovered. They made a little feast, not of food, but of beauty and colour, a thoughtful arrangement for a very sleepy badger who deserved a bit of cheer.

They waited. The forest was quiet, bathed in warm dappled sunlight that filtered through the leaves. A gentle breeze rustled the leaves above, creating a soft whispering song. Nettle sat very still on a branch, listening to the birds sing and feeling the warm sun on his fur. He watched a ladybug crawl slowly on a leaf. Nettle’s tail gave a tiny hopeful twitch, and Mr. Hugs sat perfectly still, his warm presence a quiet comfort. They had done their very best, and all they could do now was wait with hopeful little hearts.

Until finally, Iorwen the badger stirred. He stretched, letting out a mighty yawn that ruffled his thick fur and made his whiskers quiver. He blinked his sleepy eyes open. He peered out of his burrow, expecting more of the quiet morning. But then he saw it. A cluster of beautiful acorn cups, each one holding a bright splash of colour, a vibrant miniature garden. He sniffed the air, catching the sweet delicate scent of the petals, a fragrance that spoke of sunshine and happy meadows. As he looked at the bright colours, a warm feeling, like sunshine spreading through his tummy and all the way to his toes, began to bloom in his chest. He looked at Nettle, bright eyes wide with surprise and delight, and then at Mr. Hugs, whose button eyes seemed to twinkle with silent understanding. He understood perfectly.

“Oh,” Iorwen rumbled, voice soft with surprise and a deep heartwarming gratitude. “My dear friends. Nettle, Mr. Hugs… this is just lovely. What a beautiful surprise.”

Ever since then, the acorn cups stayed a little while on Iorwen’s doorstep, petals fading in the kindest way. Nettle still lined up pebbles and feathers in his nest. Mr. Hugs still sat by his window. Iorwen, when he woke, always sniffed for pink and yellow and violet first. The forest kept smelling of pine and damp earth, and the smallest cups held the biggest colours, just for a friend who had been asleep.
characters: Nettle (a squirrel), Mr. Hugs (a teddy bear)
author: StoryGen Community
